name: Puschkinia
family: Asparagaceae, the asparagus family (the hyacinth group)
grown_as: Striped squill. William's is Puschkinia scilloides var. libanotica, the usual garden form.
habit: A small plant 10 to 20 cm high: two upright leaves and one flower stem from each bulb, spreading into small clumps.

leaf.arrangement: Usually two leaves from the base, upright, facing each other and wrapping the flower stem at the bottom
leaf.outline: 10 to 15 cm long by 5 to 15 mm wide, even width
leaf.base: Wrapping the stem at soil level
leaf.surface: Smooth, slightly fleshy, a shallow channel along the middle

flower.form: Small starry bells, opening flat or slightly cupped
flower.petals: Six tepals joined at the base into a short tube, pointed oval, spreading
flower.colour: Very pale blue to white, each tepal with a clear darker blue stripe down its middle
flower.centre: A tiny pale cup (corona) in the middle made by the joined stamen stalks, with yellow anthers inside
flower.carried: Four to ten flowers in a loose spike up the top of the stem, facing out and slightly nodding

fruit: A rounded, three-lobed green capsule about 1 cm, ripening pale brown; the stem flops as it ripens.
seedling: Not drawn. A single grass-like leaf.
winter: Nothing above ground until late February.

bloom: six pale tepals each with a darker blue stripe down the middle
a small cup in the centre
bulb: a small onion-shaped bulb 1 to 2 cm
shoots: two leaves coming up together, the flower bud between them
bright green, blunt-tipped strap leaves, short at first
flower: a loose spike of four to ten pale striped stars
seedhead: round three-lobed pods along a flopping stem
the two strap leaves starting to yellow

look_alikes: Glory-of-the-snow (Scilla luciliae, once Chionodoxa) has upturned starry flowers, bluer, with a white eye and no cup. Siberian squill (Scilla siberica) has nodding deep blue bells. Both lack the stripe on each tepal.
